correctness.rationale: For identical events spaced by Δ with retention s in (0,1), the post-event map b→s(b+aΔ) contracts to aΔs/(1−s); the time average over an interval is that fixed point plus aΔ/2. Applying this directly at Δ=T and Δ=T/2 with doses 2^p x and x gives the two means. The difference has the sign of coth(x/2)/coth(2^(p−1)x)−2. The logarithmic derivative is −1/sinh(x)+2^p/sinh(2^p x), strictly negative because sinh(u)/u increases for positive u and p>0. The ratio decreases from 2^p to 1, proving strict split advantage even at p=1 and precisely one crossover with the stated orientation for p>1. At p=2 the tie reduces to cosh²(x)−cosh(x)−1=0, with exactly one positive x. The supplied finite checker was inspected, not run; the result follows for the full domain analytically. The two policies remove the same total aT per period in this model, so the conclusion is only about time-average retained mass.

value.rationale: The two prescribed policies expose competing effects of a larger dose per event and shorter dry gaps. The exact boundary tells a modeler when the direction reverses, including a domain where the one-storm policy never wins, without requiring simulation or values of a and T. This is useful within the idealized stock model, not a field recommendation, a global scheduling optimum, or a reduction in total export.
